🎯 Key Takeaways for quick navigation:

00:00 🚀 OpenAI is launching the GPT Store, offering revenue share for AI applications created without coding knowledge. Early adoption provides a significant advantage.
02:48 🏗️ The success in the GPT Store is likely to revolve around building a reputation as a "Builder" and creating a focused portfolio of GPTs that cater to specific needs or niches.
05:46 🧠 Building a suite of products with a front-end to attract new users and a back-end for returning customers is crucial. Focus on a specific area rather than chasing diverse directions.
08:08 💼 Long-term thinking, providing value, and staying focused are key to success in the GPT Store. The initial phase may seem easy, but as competition increases, adhering to these principles becomes crucial.
16:13 🌐 Creating a central hub (e.g., "home base") for all GPTs with a conversation starter helps users discover and navigate through your GPT offerings effectively in the OpenAI GPT Store.
21:02 📊 Researching popular keywords on platforms like Google helps in crafting effective names and descriptions for GPTs in the OpenAI Store.
23:09 🌐 Early adoption and having a presence in less-targeted categories, like finance, can lead to better visibility and traffic in the OpenAI GPT Store.
24:48 🎥 Creating tutorial videos and documentation can enhance user experience and understanding, adding value to GPT offerings in the OpenAI Store.
25:32 🚫 When naming GPTs, be creative and avoid using brand names. The GPT Store may not allow certain brand-related terms in the app's name.
27:20 🔗 Changing the name of a GPT app doesn't affect its functionality or accessibility, but consider SEO value and try to finalize the name early for consistency.

comments.author: @cliffordramsey2500
comments.text: I honestly think the main advantage to making GPTs right now is mostly to demonstrate clever prompting, ai knowledge, and creative applications of ai to businesses when looking for a job or selling services. The money making opportunity is likely only going to be available to a small number of people fighting in a hypercompetitive environment to maintain dominance in their niche, since you're not getting paid per GPT "download", just an undisclosed percentage of revenue to an undisclosed number of "top performers", and the barrier of entry to make a GPT is so low. Additionally this whole custom GPT phenomena in its current incarnation is most likely just a transitionary phase designed to capture the public's attention while they roll out more sophisticated agent services. That's why I think its still valuable for one's portfolio to contain custom GPTs, because it shows you're up to date with the current wave and thinking creatively with how to apply it, and are likely poised for what's coming next.
